title: Release runs both ways
statement: When a learner stumbles in independent work, step back to shared work on the same content rather than moving on, since gradual release runs both ways.
detail: One of a grade-3 reading rulebook's five laws calls release a loop: when the child stumbles unaided, step back to shared work on the same content. Its acceptance test is that, with the I-do, we-do and you-do labels stripped, the work still shows modelling, shared work and independent work of the same skill. A reading quality canon applied in a grade-5 audit adds re-entering modelling on a new genre or a harder text and calls the coached middle stage where growth happens, so release is not a one-way ratchet.
against: Another record, one-process-falling-support, holds that support across modelling, guided and independent practice only falls, and a closing-question pattern it cites says "3. Support fades and never returns." (`shadow-content-eval/references/closing_questions_pattern.md`, line 72); a review there counted support coming back as a fault (`shadow-content-eval/reports/G3-U2-L1-review.md`, line 51).

evidence.quote: Release is a LOOP: when the child stumbles unaided, step back to shared work on the same content.
Acceptance test: strip the I-do/we-do/you-do labels and the artifact must still show modelling → shared work → independent work of the SAME skill.
Re-enter I-do on a new genre or harder text; the coached we-do 'middle' is where growth happens — release is not a one-way ratchet.
